lines: Afternoon. They're eaters, mostly. Have a windfall if you like, only not off the trees. I count what's on the trees.
I'm out of the rows well before the bell. They look longer after dark. I walked one end to end once, after nine, and I don't want to say how long it took.
The top ones keep going. Right off the top branches, a few every night. Nothing I know of climbs that high. I've stopped counting the top ones.
The fence was put up for the sheep. We have not had sheep in years. I keep it mended all the same.

country_regular.speaker: A Man in a Grey Coat

lines: I've had my one. I'll have another at six. He shuts the doors at nine sharp, and he's never once let anybody stay in, not in thirty years.
People ask what it's halfway between. I've drunk here thirty years and I've never asked. It isn't that sort of question.
See the lamp by the door? He lights it at dusk and it burns till morning. I've never once seen him fill it.
The carts used to stop here and water the horses at that trough. Nobody's come through with a cart since the spring. He fills it all the same.
